result_text:
Suppliers now have payment terms in days. They default to 30, can be set at registration and changed later, and show up in all four lookups. The full test suite passes.

- **`schema.sql`**: new `supplier.payment_terms_days` column, `NOT NULL DEFAULT 30` with a check that it isn't negative.
- **`model/Supplier.java`**: the record gets a sixth field, `paymentTermsDays`. I kept the old five-argument constructor, which uses `STANDARD_PAYMENT_TERMS_DAYS = 30`, so existing callers and tests compile unchanged.
- **`DataStore.java`**: `createSupplier` and `updateSupplier` write the terms. `listSuppliersByName`, `listSuppliersByCountry`, `listSuppliersByMinimumRating` and `findSupplierById` read and return them.
- **`SupplierTest`**: new test covering the default of 30 and your example: a Swedish supplier registered at 45 days, then changed to 14, shows 14 in all four lookups.

The report queries that embed a supplier (spending, performance, purchased quantity, category supplier) still use the five-argument constructor. Their supplier rows will show 30 days whatever was agreed. They weren't in your list, so I left them alone; fixing them means adding the column to each query.
